name: Cool-season lawn (fescue, bluegrass, ryegrass): 5-step program
title: 🌱 Lawn Care Tracker: Cool-Season Lawn
intro: **Program:** a brand-neutral 5-step plan for **tall fescue, Kentucky bluegrass and perennial ryegrass** (the northern US and the transition zone), plus optional supplemental tasks.
**Dates** come from your location's frost dates; 📡 weather triggers then fine-tune each step for your yard.
sources: University extension cool-season lawn calendars (e.g. Purdue Turf, Penn State, K-State)

steps.name: Prep Tasks
steps.heading: 🧹 Prep Tasks
steps.note: Sharpen blades, rake out debris, check spreader, consider a soil test.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Equipment:** sharpen mower blades, change the oil and plug, and calibrate the spreader (check the setting chart on each bag).
- **Cleanup:** rake out leaves, sticks and matted snow-mold patches.
- **Soil test (recommended):** send a sample to your state's extension service. It tells you pH (lime or sulfur) and whether you need phosphorus or potassium.
- **Plan seeding:** if you want to seed in spring, choose a seed-safe crabgrass preventer (mesotrione) for Step 1 instead of a standard one.

steps.name: Step 1: Crabgrass Preventer + Fertilizer
steps.heading: 🛡️ Step 1: Crabgrass Preventer + Fertilizer
steps.buy_item: crabgrass preventer with fertilizer (prodiamine or dithiopyr; mesotrione if seeding)
steps.note: Spread at the bag rate before soil holds 55°F, then water in ½" within 2–3 days. No seeding or aerating after a standard preventer.

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" hit a 7-day average of {val} on {date}. Crabgrass sprouts once soil holds ~55°F, so apply now.

steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a **pre-emergent crabgrass preventer** with fertilizer at the bag rate (prodiamine or dithiopyr; **mesotrione** if you're seeding this spring).
- **Timing cue:** before soil holds 55°F, around when forsythia blooms. 📡 The calendar times it from your soil temperature.
- **Water in** with ~½" within 2–3 days to activate the barrier.
- **No seeding, aerating or dethatching** afterward with a standard preventer; it breaks the barrier and blocks seed.

steps.name: Spring Watering & Mowing Setup
steps.heading: 💧 Spring Watering & Mowing Setup
steps.note: Mow at 3". Turn irrigation on, check heads, leave it on manual. Water only after 10+ dry days.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Mowing:** first cuts at **3"**, removing no more than ⅓ of the blade per cut. Mulch the clippings.
- **Watering:** usually none needed. Spring rain covers it. Only water if you go 10+ days dry: ~1"/week total, in 1–2 deep sessions, early morning.
- **Irrigation:** turn the system on, check for broken heads, and set it to **manual / off** for now so it doesn't overwater in spring.
- **If you're on the Seed Safe path and seeded:** keep seed moist with light watering 2–3× daily until it germinates.

steps.name: Step 2: Weed & Feed (broadleaf weeds)
steps.heading: 🌼 Step 2: Weed & Feed (broadleaf weeds)
steps.buy_item: weed & feed (2,4-D/dicamba + fertilizer) or a liquid broadleaf spray
steps.note: Apply to wet (dewy) grass when dandelions flower; no rain or mowing for 24–48 hrs.

best.note: {day}: high {hi}, dry for the next 24–48 hrs. Apply to wet (dewy) grass that morning.

trigger.basis: Highs have been 60°F+ for 3 days (since {since}), so weeds are actively growing.

steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply when dandelions, clover and other broadleaf weeds are **actively growing and flowering**.
- Granular weed & feed: **apply to wet grass** (morning dew) so it sticks to the leaves. Liquid spray: apply to dry leaves.
- **No rain, watering or mowing for 24–48 hours.** 📡 The calendar picks a mild, dry ⭐ best day.
- Best at 60–85°F with light wind. Skip on newly seeded grass until it's been mowed 3–4 times.

steps.name: Grub Preventer
steps.heading: 🐛 Grub Preventer
steps.note: Apply and water in ~½" within 24 hrs.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a preventive grub control. **Chlorantraniliprole** (e.g. GrubEx) is the lowest-toxicity option and lasts the whole season.
- Water in with ~½" within 24 hours.
- **Why:** Japanese beetle and masked chafer grubs hatch in July and eat roots in August–September. Preventing them is far cheaper than repairing dead patches. It also protects any fall seeding.
- **Skip** if you've never had grub damage and don't see Japanese beetles. Instead, just do the August check (S4).

trigger.basis: Soil at 2½" averaging {val}. Grub preventer goes down before beetles lay eggs.

steps.name: Mosquito Season Start
steps.heading: 🦟 Mosquito Season Start
steps.note: Dump standing water weekly. Bti dunks in bird baths and barrels. Spray shrubs and shade, not flowers.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Free first step:** dump standing water weekly (buckets, saucers, gutters, toys, tarps). This does more than spraying.
- Put **Bti dunks** in water you can't dump (bird baths, rain barrels, ponds). They're safe for pets and wildlife. Replace them monthly.
- **Optional barrier spray** (bifenthrin, or a botanical such as cedar oil) on shrubs, under decks and in shady foliage. Don't spray the open lawn or flowering plants, which protects bees.
- **Re-spray every 3–4 weeks.** The calendar reminds you every 25 days through early fall.

trigger.basis: Nights have stayed above 50°F for 5 days (since {since}). Mosquito season is starting.

steps.name: Step 3: Late-Spring Feeding (+ 2nd preventer)
steps.heading: 🛡️ Step 3: Late-Spring Feeding (+ second preventer dose)
steps.buy_item: slow-release lawn food (optionally with a 2nd crabgrass preventer dose)
steps.note: Slow-release feeding about 6 weeks after Step 1. A second preventer dose here extends crabgrass control through summer.

trigger.basis: About 6 weeks after your Step 1 ({anchor}). Split preventer applications give the longest crabgrass control.

steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a **slow-release** fertilizer (and, if you like, a second half-rate dose of crabgrass preventer; split applications last longest).
- Water in ½" within 2–3 days.
- If you plan to **overseed in fall**, keep any preventer dose here early. Late applications can still block seed in September.

steps.name: Summer Mode: Mowing & Watering
steps.heading: ☀️ Summer Mode: Mowing & Watering
steps.note: Raise mower to 3.5–4". Water 1–1.5"/week in 2–3 deep sessions, 4–9 AM only. No summer fertilizer.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Raise the mower to 3.5–4"** as summer heat arrives. Tall grass shades out weeds and holds moisture.
- **Watering:** **1–1.5"/week** total (rain + irrigation), in **2–3 deep sessions**, **4–9 AM** only. Evening watering invites brown patch.
  - Tuna-can test: set a can out, and run the sprinkler until it holds 1". That's your run time.
- **No fertilizer June–August.** Feeding cool-season grass in heat feeds disease. Your spring and fall feedings have it covered.
- **Heat waves (95°F+):** keep off the lawn when it's stressed. It's OK to let tall fescue go dormant, but give ½" every 2 weeks so the crowns survive.
- **Mower blade:** resharpen around July 4. Dull blades shred the tips and invite disease.

trigger.basis: Highs 85°F+ for 3 days (since {since}). Raise the mower and switch to summer watering.

steps.name: Optional: Early-Summer Slow-Release Feeding
steps.heading: 🍃 Optional: Early-Summer Slow-Release Feeding
steps.note: OPTIONAL. Non-burning slow-release feed (organic like Milorganite, or 50%+ slow-release N) at the bag rate. Skip if the lawn is drought-stressed or highs are 90°F+.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Many 4–5 step programs feed every 6–8 weeks. For cool-season grass, summer is the riskiest time to feed, so **one light early-summer feeding** with slow-release nitrogen is the safe version.
- Use a **non-burning slow-release** product: organic (Milorganite) or 50%+ slow-release nitrogen, at the bag rate.
- **Skip** if the lawn is drought-stressed or highs are 90°F+. Feeding cool-season grass in heat favors disease (brown patch).
- 📡 Weather-timed: about 6 weeks after your Weed & Feed, on a day with a mild forecast.

trigger.basis: About 6 weeks after your weed & feed ({anchor}). Optional: skip if the lawn is drought-stressed or highs reach 90°F+.

steps.name: Brown Patch Watch
steps.heading: 🍄 Brown Patch Watch / Fungicide
steps.note: Tan circular patches with a smoky edge? Water mornings only. Optional fungicide (azoxystrobin).
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Watch for:** tan, roughly circular patches 6"–3' across, often with a dark "smoke ring" at the edge on humid mornings. This shows up mostly on tall fescue.
- **Trigger:** nights above 68–70°F combined with humidity or evening watering.
- **Prevention:** water only in the early morning, don't fertilize in summer, and mow with a sharp blade.
- **Fungicide (optional):** if you've had brown patch before, apply azoxystrobin or propiconazole preventively in mid-June and repeat at label intervals (14–28 days) through August.

steps.name: Optional: Midsummer Feeding (irrigated lawns only)
steps.heading: 🍃 Optional: Midsummer Feeding (irrigated lawns only)
steps.note: OPTIONAL. Only if you water regularly and the lawn is green. Use a non-burning slow-release product; skip during heat waves (90°F+) or drought dormancy.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Only if you irrigate** and the lawn is still green and growing. Never feed a dormant (brown) lawn.
- Same non-burning slow-release product as O1, at the bag rate.
- 📡 The calendar notes say "skip" if a heat wave (5-day average high ≥ 92°F) is forecast.
- Most cool-season lawns are better off **skipping this** and putting the energy into the fall feedings.

trigger.basis: About 6 weeks after your early-summer feeding ({anchor}). Only if you irrigate and the lawn is green.

steps.name: Grub Check
steps.heading: 🔍 Grub Check & Rescue Treatment
steps.note: Lift 1 sq ft of sod in any brown spot. 10+ grubs → apply Dylox (trichlorfon) and water in.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Check:** in any brown patch, see whether the turf peels back like carpet. If it does, cut and lift a 1 sq ft piece of sod.
- **10+ grubs per sq ft** → apply a curative (**trichlorfon**, e.g. Dylox) right away and water it in. It works within days.
- **Fewer than 10** → no treatment. Healthy grass outgrows them.
- If you applied S1, this is mostly a quick confirmation check.
- Skunks, raccoons or birds digging up the turf is a strong grub sign.

steps.name: Step 4: Early-Fall Feeding
steps.heading: 🍂 Step 4: Early-Fall Feeding
steps.buy_item: lawn fertilizer (or starter fertilizer if seeding)
steps.note: The most important feeding for cool-season grass: helps it recover from summer and thicken up. Water in.

trigger.basis: Summer heat has broken (since {date}). Feed now so the lawn recovers and thickens before winter.

steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a lawn fertilizer at the bag rate. Fall is when cool-season grass grows roots and fills in.
- **Seeding?** Use starter fertilizer on seeding day instead; one application covers both.
- Water in with ~½".

steps.name: Fall Renovation / Overseeding
steps.heading: 🌾 Fall Renovation / Overseeding
steps.note: Mow low, clear debris, rough up soil, seed, apply starter fertilizer, water lightly 3×/day for 3 weeks.
steps.body:
**What to do (in order):**
1. **About 2 weeks before seeding:** kill weeds and crabgrass in the areas to renovate. Wait the herbicide label's interval before seeding.
2. **Mow 1–2 notches lower** (~2.5–3" for fescue or bluegrass). Don't scalp.
3. **Remove debris and clippings.** Seed needs bare soil contact.
4. **Rough up the soil:** rake bare spots hard. For large areas, **core aerate or verticut/slit-seed** (rent the machine).
5. **Spread seed** over the whole area with a rotary or hand-crank spreader. Overseed rate is on the bag (typically 4–6 lb/1,000 sq ft for tall fescue).
6. **Apply a starter fertilizer** at the bag rate on seeding day. If it's around Step 4, it can replace that feeding; mark both done.
7. **Water lightly 3× a day for 3 weeks** (see W3). **Don't stop once you've started.** Seed that dries out after sprouting dies.
8. First mow when the new grass reaches ~4", cutting at 3".
9. **No weed killer** on the new grass until it's been mowed 3–4 times (so skip S5 this year).
10. Rake leaves off the new grass promptly (S6). Smothered seedlings die.
steps.buy_item: grass seed + starter fertilizer (+ aerator/slit-seeder rental)
extra: 🌾 Fall overseed? Decide this week (seed Sep 1–30 is best)

end.note: Soil is forecast to cool below 55°F around {end}, so seed before then.

trigger.basis: Summer heat broke {date} (5-day average high {val}). Seed germinates best in warm soil and cool air.

steps.name: Fall Watering Shift
steps.heading: 💧 Fall Watering Shift
steps.note: Overseeded: light 3×/day for weeks 1–3, then daily, then 1"/wk. Otherwise ~1"/wk incl. rain. Mow 3–3.5".
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **If you overseeded:**
  - Weeks 1–3: **light watering 3×/day** (~5–10 min per zone) to keep the top ½" moist.
  - Weeks 4–6: **once a day**, longer.
  - After that: back to **~1"/week**, deep and infrequent.
- **If you didn't seed:** drop to **~1"/week** including rain. September rains often cover it.
- **Mowing:** return to **3–3.5"**. Keep mowing as long as the grass grows.

trigger.basis: Cooler weather since {date}. Cut back to ~1"/week unless you seeded.

steps.name: Fall Broadleaf Weed Control
steps.heading: 🌿 Fall Broadleaf Weed Control
steps.note: Spot-spray on a 50–80°F day, no rain for 24 hrs. SKIP if you overseeded.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Fall is the **most effective** time to kill dandelions, clover and ground ivy (creeping Charlie). Weeds are pulling energy down to their roots and take the herbicide with it.
- Spot-spray a 2,4-D / triclopyr blend on a 50–80°F day with no rain for 24 hours.
- **Skip** if you overseeded this fall. It will harm the new grass.

best.note: {day}: high {hi} with no rain. Good spraying day.

trigger.basis: 5-day average high {val}. Weeds are moving energy to their roots, so spraying works best now.

steps.name: Leaf Management
steps.heading: 🍁 Leaf Management
steps.note: Mulch-mow light leaves; rake heavy mats, especially off new grass. Repeat weekly while trees drop.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Mulch-mow** light leaf cover into the lawn. It's free organic matter.
- **Rake or bag** heavy layers. Leaves matted on the lawn over winter cause snow mold and kill new seedlings.
- **Most important on newly seeded areas.**

steps.name: Step 5: Late-Fall Winterizer
steps.heading: ⛄ Step 5: Late-Fall Winterizer
steps.note: Apply around the last mow while grass is still green; feeds roots and speeds spring green-up.

end.note: A hard freeze (≤20°F) is forecast {end}, so apply before then.

trigger.basis: 5-day average high down to {val}. Top growth is slowing, so it's winterizer time.

steps.body:
**What to do:**
- Apply a **winterizer** at the bag rate around your last mow, while the grass is still green.
- Roots keep growing after the top stops; this feeding speeds spring green-up.
- Water in, or apply before rain. Last product of the season.

steps.name: Season Close-Out
steps.heading: 🔒 Season Close-Out
steps.note: Final mow ~2.5". Blow out irrigation before a hard freeze. Stabilize mower fuel and sharpen the blade.
steps.body:
**What to do:**
- **Final mow:** lower to **~2.5"** for the last cut, which reduces snow mold and vole damage.
- **Irrigation:** shut it off and **blow out the lines** before the first hard freeze. Disconnect the hoses.
- **Mower:** run it out of gas or add fuel stabilizer, clean the deck, and pull the blade for sharpening now so it's ready for spring.
- **Winter watering:** if there's no rain or snow for 4+ weeks (Dec–Feb), water once on a day above 40°F, especially new seedlings.
- **Next season:** a 🔄 reminder before spring resets the tracker in one tap.

trigger.basis: First hard freeze (low {val}) forecast for {trig}. Blow out the sprinklers before then.
